rappel_detail.anchor: slung block at the notch (two tat anchors to choose from)
rappel_detail.station: The belay notch below the summit slab, after downclimbing or top-roping the leader off the summit; there is no anchor on the summit itself.
rappel_detail.notes: The one rappel, on a single 60 m rope, below the steepest, loosest part of the gully. Some parties split it into two using an intermediate anchor lower down.
hazards: Tat anchors: inspect and back up. The gully is loose.

set.rappels: Descend the West Route gully: one single-rope rappel from slung blocks at the notch. Rappelling Beckey-Tate itself takes five or six two-rope rappels off slings and trees through loose rock, and most parties avoid it.
set.descent_text: Do not plan to rappel the Beckey-Tate line itself — while it's technically possible with two ropes (roughly five or six rappels off slings and trees), the route wanders and holds a lot of large loose rock, making rope-stuck and rockfall risk high; most parties explicitly avoid it. Instead, from the top of the route scramble about 20 ft up and left to the notch between the south face and the true summit, which stands a few hundred feet higher. To tag it, drop about 150 ft of scree on the far side, cross north into the West Route gully and climb its short pitches to the unprotected 5.6 summit slab (protected by a single old bolt), which is downclimbed or top-roped; then descend the shared gully: two slung-block anchors get you down with one or two single-rope rappels (a 60m rope is sufficient either way) through the steep/loose upper gully, after which it's a scree-and-snow walk/glissade down the gully back to the approach basin, across Early Winters Creek, and out the climbers' trail to the Hairpin Turn. Expect the full descent to take a couple of hours; keep helmets on throughout given the loose rock in the gully.
